site.name: vaultkey
site.summary: vaultkey-clone Fictional password manager "Vaultkey" — short marketing landing + main pricing page. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero with title / dual CTAs; faux app screenshot (categorized sidebar + searchable item list with passkey / family / 2FA tags); 7-name trust strip; 3 why-cards; bottom CTA | | `pricing.html` | Main page: yearly / monthly billing toggle (annual saves 20%); 3 plan cards (Personal $0 forever, Family $3.99/mo featured, Business per-seat); **Business per-seat slider 3–200 with linked number input**, 5-tier volume pricing (3–24 / 25–49 / 50–99 / 100–199 / 200+) with monthly + yearly totals; enterprise contact strip; 25-row grouped feature comparison table (5 groups: Vault & sync / Sharing / Security / Admin & compliance / Support); 8-question FAQ accordion | | `styles.css` | Brand color #1E1B4B indigo + #A3E635 lime accent; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 2 breakpoints (>1000 / <1000 / <640) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full vaultkey system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Vaultkey landing and pricing pages present a clean aesthetic but suffer from significant mobile layout and logic issues. On mobile viewports, the feature comparison table causes horizontal page overflow, and header navigation elements like 'Sign in' wrap awkwardly with undersized tap targets. Additionally, state desynchronization issues—such as the business seat input failing to clamp large values and billing frequency text failing to update on the monthly view—undermine trust and clarity.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the Vaultkey marketing and pricing pages, focusing heavily on the interactive pricing calculators and responsive layout.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will begin by validating the landing page CTAs and layout. It will then deeply test the pricing page's interactive elements, including the yearly/monthly billing toggle, the business seat slider, and the linked number input. Finally, it will check the FAQ accordion and perform mobile viewport validations to assess tap targets and responsive design.
assumptions: The business seat slider and number input are bidirectionally linked and dynamically update the displayed price based on volume tiers.
The yearly/monthly toggle updates prices globally across all plan cards.
The FAQ section uses accordion controls to expand/collapse answers.
risk_hotspots: Bidirectional sync between the range slider and number input for Business seats.
Dynamic price calculations reflecting both the complex volume tiers and billing frequency.
Navigation and CTA tap targets on mobile viewports (flagged as small in prescan).

phases.title: Landing Page Validation
phases.objective: Verify the structure, navigation, and primary CTAs on the landing page.
key_checks: Check presence and visibility of main navigation links.
Verify 'See plans' and 'Pricing' links successfully route to pricing.html.
exit_criteria: Navigation is confirmed functional and structural elements are present.

phases.title: Pricing Billing Toggle
phases.objective: Test the Yearly/Monthly billing toggle state and its effect on prices.
key_checks: Toggle to 'Monthly' and observe price updates on Family and Business plans.
Toggle back to 'Yearly' and confirm the 20% discount is applied correctly.
exit_criteria: Prices correctly reflect the selected billing frequency on all affected plan cards.

phases.title: Business Seat Calculator
phases.objective: Validate the slider and number input logic for Business plan pricing.
key_checks: Change the range slider value and verify the number input updates synchronously.
Type a valid number (e.g., 50) into the input and verify the slider and total price update.
Test boundary values (e.g., <3 or >200) to check error handling or clamping.
Observe if price calculation matches the specific volume tiers (3-24, 25-49, etc.).
exit_criteria: Slider and input stay synced, and prices calculate correctly based on volume tiers and boundaries.

phases.title: Feature Table and FAQ Interaction
phases.objective: Ensure the comparison table is readable and FAQ accordions function as intended.
key_checks: Scroll through the 25-row feature comparison table to ensure groups are well-structured.
Click multiple FAQ accordion headers to verify expand/collapse behavior and content visibility.
exit_criteria: FAQ items can be toggled open and closed without layout breakage.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness
phases.objective: Check layout and tap targets in a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Assess navigation menu stacking or hamburger menu presence.
Verify slider usability and table horizontal scrolling on narrow screens.
Investigate the small tap targets reported in the prescan.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout is functionally evaluated and tap target issues are documented.

coverage_targets.features: Thoroughly exercise the billing toggle, seat slider, linked number input, and FAQ accordions.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate layout and interaction of the pricing calculator and navigation on mobile viewports.

notes: The user goal mentioned a settings/privacy flow, but the site directory only contains marketing/pricing pages. The plan focuses on the available interactive elements while ensuring deep validation of the complex pricing logic.

findings.user_goal: Calculate business plan pricing based on team size.
findings.problem: The business seat calculator number input does not restrict or clamp entered values beyond its maximum limit (e.g., typing '300' into the input field).
findings.evidence: Session memory notes: 'The seat calculator number input allows entering values beyond its maximum (e.g., typing '300'), but it does not auto-clamp the displayed input value.'
findings.why_it_matters: Allowing invalid numbers without correction creates a desynchronization between the displayed input value and the actual calculated price, misleading users about volume pricing limits.
findings.suggestion: Add validation logic to auto-clamp the input to the defined maximum (e.g., 200) on blur or during input.

findings.user_goal: Compare plan features on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The 'Compare every feature' table is too wide for mobile viewports, causing the entire page to overflow horizontally.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings report 'Page width 426px exceeds viewport 390px', and trajectory notes confirm the 'BUSINESS' column is cut off on mobile.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal page scrolling disrupts vertical reading flow and makes it frustrating to navigate back and forth to compare feature availability.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the feature comparison table in a dedicated horizontally scrollable container (`overflow-x: auto`), or stack the comparison data vertically for mobile viewports.
findings.source_hint: table or container for 'Compare every feature'

findings.user_goal: Understand monthly pricing vs yearly pricing.
findings.problem: When the billing toggle is switched to 'Monthly', the descriptive subtitle under the Family plan incorrectly continues to say 'Billed yearly'.
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunk notes: 'The Yearly/Monthly toggle updates the plan prices... but the billing frequency subtitle under the Family plan price incorrectly remains Billed yearly'.
findings.why_it_matters: Contradictory pricing copy during plan selection creates doubt and erodes trust right before the user decides to convert.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the subtitle text dynamically updates to 'Billed monthly' when the Monthly toggle is active, or remove the frequency text if it is redundant.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to the sign-in page on mobile.
findings.problem: The 'Sign in' link in the mobile header wraps awkwardly onto two lines and has a small touch area.
findings.evidence: Observed in the mobile screenshot (agentic-49-click-mobile.png) where 'Sign' sits above 'in', and layout warnings flag its tap target as only 33x32px.
findings.why_it_matters: Text wrapping in tight header spaces looks unprofessional, and the resulting small tap area makes the link difficult to activate reliably on touchscreens.
findings.suggestion: Adjust mobile header padding or allocate more flex-basis width for the 'Sign in' link so it remains on a single line with at least a 44x44px tap area.

findings.user_goal: Adjust the team size using a screen reader.
findings.problem: The number input adjacent to the business seat range slider lacks an accessible label.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings detect 'A form field has no label, aria-label, or placeholder' (target_id: ux-9).
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users traversing form controls will land on this input without knowing it controls the 'Team size' or seat count.
findings.suggestion: Add an `aria-label="Number of seats"` to the number input field.

findings.user_goal: Expand FAQ questions using assistive technology.
findings.problem: The FAQ accordion buttons contain a hardcoded '▼' character in the DOM and lack `aria-expanded` attributes to communicate their state.
findings.evidence: Trajectory notes: 'The arrow in the button's accessible name remains '▼' even when expanded, likely because it is hardcoded in the HTML'.
findings.why_it_matters: Without `aria-expanded`, screen reader users cannot programmatically determine if an accordion panel is currently open or closed.
findings.suggestion: Implement `aria-expanded="true/false"` on the accordion triggers and use CSS/SVG for the chevron icons rather than hardcoded text characters.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the page and toggle billing options easily on a phone.
findings.problem: Multiple key navigational and interactive elements have heights well below standard mobile touch target recommendations.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag the Vaultkey logo (30px high), 'Yearly' toggle (32px high), and 'Monthly' toggle (32px high).
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized buttons require higher precision to tap, increasing the likelihood of missed taps or activating the wrong control on small screens.
findings.suggestion: Apply a minimum height of 44px to all primary navigation links, buttons, and billing toggles on mobile viewports.

gaps: 52% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
